rv.q: This play is nothing less than the most articulate and utterly hilarious original production I have seen since the pandemic ended.
Julian Hester’s terrific production of this incredibly funny farcical take on Shakespearian comedies is nothing but pure delight.
The Artistic Home presents a sidesplitting farce with playwright Siah Berlatsky's Malapert Love.
If this is what Berlatsky can do on a crowded el train, the world has much more to look forward to from this writer.
"Malapert Love" has a lot to say about economic class struggle and the contradictory nature of love, but it’s what it doesn’t need to say that rings loudest.
